title: Work IQ: business skills for agents through Work IQ MCP
summary: The briefing passes: the roadmap facts, qualified new-environment default, billing treatment and documented controls are supported. Two control paths stop before the final setting, and the Cowork credit statement needs an additional citation; these are minor corrections.

claims.claim: The roadmap status is In development.
claims.quote: "status": "In development", "statusKey": "in-development"

claims.claim: The roadmap target is November CY2026.
claims.quote: "targetDate": "November CY2026"

claims.claim: The roadmap preview target is September CY2026.
claims.quote: "previewDate": "September CY2026"

claims.claim: The roadmap lists General Availability and Preview release phases.
claims.quote: "releasePhase": ["General Availability", "Preview"]

claims.claim: The roadmap lists Worldwide (Standard Multi-Tenant).
claims.quote: "clouds": ["Worldwide (Standard Multi-Tenant)"]

claims.claim: The roadmap platform is Web.
claims.quote: "platforms": ["Web"]

claims.claim: The roadmap products are Microsoft Copilot (Microsoft 365), Microsoft Dataverse and Work IQ.
claims.quote: "products": ["Microsoft Copilot (Microsoft 365)", "Microsoft Dataverse", "Work IQ"]

claims.claim: Business skills are natural-language instructions capturing organisational processes, policies and domain knowledge.
claims.quote: Business skills are natural-language instructions that capture how your organization gets work done. They represent your business processes, policies, and domain knowledge in a format that agents can understand and follow.

claims.claim: A skill describes the steps, required information and business rules for completing work.
claims.quote: Each skill describes how to complete a specific type of work—the steps involved, the information required, and the business rules that apply.

claims.claim: Agents discover and use accessible skills as needed at runtime through Work IQ MCP.
claims.quote: Agents discover and use the business skills they have access to as needed at runtime using Work IQ MCP to complete tasks according to your organization's processes.

claims.claim: Multiple agents using the same skill follow the same process definition.
claims.quote: When multiple agents use the same skill, they follow the same process, ensuring consistent behavior across your organization.

claims.claim: Business skills are stored in Dataverse.
claims.quote: Business skills are stored in Dataverse and follow Dataverse security patterns.

claims.claim: Skill frontmatter contains a name, description and metadata.
claims.quote: Frontmatter | Name, description, and optional key-value metadata

claims.claim: The instructions layer contains the full skill body.
claims.quote: Instructions | Full skill body | Contains the complete process definition

claims.where: What's changing; Risk assessment: Data exposure
claims.claim: Skills can have attached resource files containing supporting process or policy material.
claims.quote: Resources | Attached reference files | Provides supporting documents, templates, policies, and other materials agents can use when following the skill

claims.claim: Agents query frontmatter to discover relevant skills.
claims.quote: Agents query frontmatter to find applicable skills, then retrieve full instructions and resources only when needed.

claims.claim: Agents retrieve full skill instructions only when needed.
claims.quote: Agents query frontmatter to find applicable skills, then retrieve full instructions and resources only when needed.

claims.claim: Business skills are not executable code.
claims.quote: Business skills are not executable code. They contain natural-language instructions that guide agent behavior

claims.where: front matter: defaultState; What's changing; Why it matters; Scope
claims.claim: The default is on for eligible new public production environments, subject to the stated exceptions.
claims.quote: Business Applications in Work IQ is on by default for new public production environments created for new or existing tenants. The following environments are exceptions:

claims.claim: The new-environment default covers environments created for both new and existing tenants.
claims.quote: Business Applications in Work IQ is on by default for new public production environments created for new or existing tenants.

claims.claim: Microsoft deferred the previously documented November 2026 automatic enablement plan for eligible existing environments.
claims.quote: The plan to turn on Business Applications in Work IQ for existing environments that aren't listed as exceptions has been deferred from the previously documented November 2026 schedule.

claims.claim: The current default-settings page gives no replacement date for enabling existing environments.
claims.quote: Searched: Business Applications Work IQ default existing environments deferred date EU EFTA; opened default-settings and manage-participation. The former says the November schedule is deferred and to check for updates, without a replacement date.

claims.claim: The documented automatic-enablement default applies to public production environments.
claims.quote: Business Applications in Work IQ is on by default for new public production environments

claims.claim: EU and EFTA environments are exceptions to the default enablement.
claims.quote: European Union (EU) and European Free Trade Association (EFTA) environments: This exception applies to environments provisioned in the EU and EFTA macro region geography.

claims.claim: Government-related environments are exceptions to the default enablement.
claims.quote: Government-related environments: This exception applies to environments provisioned by customers with current or previous government cloud deployments that are likely to depend on FedRAMP security controls.

claims.claim: Trial, sandbox and developer environments are exceptions to the default enablement.
claims.quote: Nonproduction environments: This exception applies to trial, sandbox, and developer environments.

claims.claim: Customers can enable Work IQ for EU and EFTA environments by enabling the tenant and environment settings.
claims.quote: If Business Applications in Work IQ isn't on by default in your environment, you can turn it on. Turn on the tenant-level setting in the Microsoft 365 admin center and the environment-level setting in the Power Platform admin center.

claims.where: What's changing; Why it matters; Scope
claims.claim: A Power Platform administrator can manually enable Work IQ in an environment for business skills.
claims.quote: To enable business skills in a Dataverse environment, a Power Platform administrator turns on Work IQ.

claims.claim: The general feature-settings reference lists the Dataverse intelligence (Work IQ) setting default as Off.
claims.quote: Turn on Dataverse intelligence (Work IQ) for agents and AI experiences | When On, allows reusable business context business skills to be used by your agents. | Off

claims.claim: Microsoft Learn describes business skills in preview documentation.
claims.quote: Dataverse intelligence (preview) ... [This section is prerelease documentation and is subject to change.]

claims.claim: The default-settings page includes prerelease documentation.
claims.quote: This is a preview feature. Preview offerings are provided as-is and may be modified or discontinued at any time.

claims.claim: Work IQ must be enabled in a Dataverse environment for business skills to be used there.
claims.quote: A Dataverse environment with Work IQ enabled by a Power Platform administrator.

claims.where: Why it matters; Governance guidance: At rollout
claims.claim: Agent selection of a skill is probabilistic.
claims.quote: Agent selection is probabilistic, so test representative requests before you share a skill broadly.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Security & identity; Governance controls
claims.claim: Dataverse ownership, sharing and security roles govern skill access, creation and modification.
claims.quote: Governance—Control who can create, modify, and use business skills through ownership, sharing, and Dataverse security roles.

claims.claim: Skill sharing controls who can read the skill and its resources.
claims.quote: The agent searches the connected environment for skills that the current identity can access. ... The agent retrieves the complete instructions and resources for a relevant skill.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Security & identity; Governance controls
claims.claim: Security-role sharing requires users to have both the selected role and Skill Sharing Role.
claims.quote: Users who access a skill through a Dataverse security role must have both the selected role and the Skill Sharing Role security role.

claims.claim: General access and direct sharing are separate skill-access methods from security-role access.
claims.quote: You can provide access to a business skill in three ways: General access ... Security role access ... Direct access

claims.where: Risk assessment: Autonomy & actions; rationale: risk
claims.claim: Skill instructions guide agents' actions with their connected tools.
claims.quote: The agent retrieves the complete instructions and resources for a relevant skill. ... The agent uses its connected tools to carry out the process.

claims.claim: Activating an updated skill changes the version agents use.
claims.quote: Save and activate | Makes your changes the active version, including its associated resources. The previous active version remains in version history.

claims.claim: Editing and saving a working copy does not change the active version.
claims.quote: Save | Saves your working copy without changing the version agents use. A new skill remains inactive. If the skill already has an active version, that version stays active.

claims.claim: Licensing is mixed, with licensed chat grounding included and consumption charged through the consuming experience.
claims.quote: The applicable entitlement includes business-data grounding in the licensed chat scenario. You don't pay extra for it as a Work IQ API interaction. ... Work IQ consumption that supports a Cowork task is attributed to Cowork.

claims.where: Cost and licensing; front matter: licensing.notes
claims.claim: Billing follows the experience that accesses the business context.
claims.quote: For Business Applications in Work IQ, you track cost by the experiences people use rather than by a dedicated business applications category.

claims.where: Cost and licensing; front matter: licensing.notes; rationale: cost
claims.claim: Licensed Microsoft 365 Copilot Chat business-data grounding is included in the applicable entitlement.
claims.quote: Microsoft 365 Copilot Chat: The applicable entitlement includes business-data grounding in the licensed chat scenario.

claims.claim: Licensed chat business-data grounding is not charged extra as a Work IQ API interaction.
claims.quote: You don't pay extra for it as a Work IQ API interaction.

claims.where: Cost and licensing; front matter: licensing.notes
claims.claim: Work IQ consumption supporting a Cowork task is attributed to Cowork.
claims.quote: Copilot Cowork: Work IQ consumption that supports a Cowork task is attributed to Cowork.

claims.where: Cost and licensing; front matter: licensing.notes
claims.claim: Coding-agent and custom-integration calls directly to Work IQ are reported under Work IQ API.
claims.quote: Coding agents or custom integrations that call Work IQ directly: Consumption through that connection appears under Work IQ API.

claims.claim: Work IQ API usage consumes Copilot Credits shared with other eligible services.
claims.quote: Work IQ API usage consumes Copilot Credits shared with other eligible services.

claims.claim: Underlying application-service licence fees may continue during the preview for consumption-based services.
claims.quote: For consumption-based services, usage of underlying application services may continue to incur license fees during the preview period.

claims.claim: No pricing or credit rate specific to business skills is published.
claims.quote: Searched: business skills Work IQ pricing Copilot Credits rate licensing; opened understand-costs, Work IQ overview, API overview and Microsoft's Work IQ GA licensing news. General API rates are published, but none is specific to business skills.

claims.claim: Skills are used in Copilot, Work IQ-connected agents and agents connected directly to Dataverse MCP.
claims.quote: Copilot and connected agents can discover and use active business skills they have access to ... Agents connected directly to the Dataverse MCP server can also discover and use business skills.

claims.claim: Business Applications in Work IQ is currently unavailable in sovereign or government clouds, including DoD, GCC and GCC High.
claims.quote: Business Applications in Work IQ isn't currently available in sovereign or government cloud environments, including Department of Defense (DoD), Government Community Cloud (GCC), and GCC High.

claims.claim: Environment Work IQ participation is controlled in Power Platform admin center at Manage > environment > Settings > Product > Features > Work IQ.
claims.quote: Select Manage, and select the environment. ... Select Settings > Product > Features. ... Locate Work IQ. ... Turn on Work IQ if it's currently off.

claims.where: controls[0].api; Governance controls: first row and API absence statement
claims.claim: Microsoft Learn documents no API equivalent for the environment Work IQ feature setting as of November 2026.
claims.quote: Searched: Work IQ environment enable setting API Power Platform API pac admin PowerShell Dataverse organization intelligence; Work IQ organization Web API settings enable. Opened manage-participation, settings-features and CLI reference; no operation for this setting was documented.

claims.claim: Tenant business-data availability is controlled at Microsoft 365 admin center > Copilot > Settings > View all > Business Applications data in Work IQ available to Copilot.
claims.quote: select Copilot > Settings. ... select View all > Business Applications data in Work IQ available to Copilot. ... To turn off access for everyone, select No users.
claims.fix: The path reaches the correct settings pane but stops before the audience control. In controls[1].ui.path and the rendered row, use 'Copilot > Settings > View all > Business Applications data in Work IQ available to Copilot > No users' to show the tenant-wide off setting documented at https://learn.microsoft.com/power-platform/admin/business-applications-work-iq/default-settings#cascading-control-settings.

claims.where: controls[1].api; Governance controls: second row and API absence statement
claims.claim: Microsoft Learn documents no API for the tenant Business Applications data in Work IQ available to Copilot audience setting as of November 2026.
claims.quote: Searched: Business Applications data in Work IQ available to Copilot tenant setting Microsoft Graph API; Business Applications data Copilot Graph settings API. Opened default-settings, copilotAdminSetting and copilotPolicySetting; the supported settings do not include this control.

claims.claim: Allowed MCP Clients is reached through Manage > Environments > environment > Settings > Product > Features > Dataverse Model Context Protocol > Advanced Settings > Allowed MCP Clients.
claims.quote: In the Dataverse Model Context Protocol section, select Go to Advanced Settings. ... In Advanced Settings > Allowed MCP Clients, open Enterprise Copilot Platform, set Is Enabled to No
claims.fix: The path reaches the correct client list but stops before its control. In controls[2].ui.path and the rendered row, use 'Manage > Environments > environment > Settings > Product > Features > Dataverse Model Context Protocol > Go to Advanced Settings > Allowed MCP Clients > client > Is Enabled', as documented at https://learn.microsoft.com/microsoft-sales-copilot/business-skills-dataverse#enable-business-skills-in-dataverse.

claims.claim: PATCH [organization URI]/api/data/v9.2/allowedmcpclients({allowedmcpclientid}) updates an allowed MCP client record.
claims.quote: Entity set path: [organization URI]/api/data/v9.2/allowedmcpclients ... Primary key: allowedmcpclientid ... Operations supported: POSTGETPATCHDELETE

claims.claim: The request-body property isenabled can be set to false to disable an allowed MCP client.
claims.quote: isenabled | Edm.Boolean | Display name: Is Enabled ... 1 | Yes ... 0 | No

claims.claim: Tenant-wide Work IQ MCP server access can be blocked at Microsoft 365 admin center > Agents > Tools > Work IQ MCP > Block.
claims.quote: Sign in to the Microsoft 365 admin center. ... Select Agents > Tools. ... Select Work IQ MCP. ... To block access to the server, select Block.

claims.where: controls[3].api; Governance controls: fourth row and API absence statement
claims.claim: Microsoft Learn documents no API for the Microsoft 365 Work IQ MCP server availability control as of November 2026.
claims.quote: Searched: Work IQ MCP server Block Agents Tools Microsoft Graph API availability; Work IQ MCP block graph availability API. Opened manage-ai-experience-access, API overview and copilotPolicySetting; results gave server UI blocking, not its API.

claims.claim: The tenant setting is part of a cascading control hierarchy over environment features.
claims.quote: You manage Business Applications in Work IQ through a cascading set of settings at three levels ... It must be on for environments to use Work IQ capabilities.

claims.claim: Power Apps lets users share a skill by selecting the skill and Share.
claims.quote: Select a skill, and then select Share from the command bar or the three-dot menu

claims.claim: Manage access shows who has skill access and permits changing or removing that access.
claims.quote: Select Manage access to review who has access, change access levels, or remove access.

claims.claim: The Dataverse CLI command dataverse mcp allow <appId> allows an application as an MCP client.
claims.quote: Ensure that a Microsoft Entra application is in the Dataverse MCP allowed clients list for the current profile's environment. ... dataverse mcp allow <appId> [options] ... The <appId> argument is the application (client) ID to allow, as a GUID.

claims.claim: The linked quickstart walks through setting up an environment for a Business Applications in Work IQ pilot.
claims.quote: You choose a pilot scenario, confirm availability, enable Work IQ in your environment, configure your model-driven app, and try the experience.

claims.claim: The cost is variable because Work IQ API use is metered in Copilot Credits.
claims.quote: Work IQ cost is variable based on usage ... Work IQ API usage consumes Copilot Credits shared with other eligible services.

claims.claim: Cowork use consumes Copilot Credits.
claims.quote: Copilot Cowork, Copilot Studio agents, and Work IQ API can consume Copilot credits from a shared tenant pool.
claims.fix: Add https://learn.microsoft.com/plugins/cost-considerations#manage-shared-copilot-credits to sources as 'Plan licensing and cost', kind 'learn', to support the existing rationale's Cowork Copilot Credits statement.

claims.where: Open questions: EU and EFTA default-enablement date
claims.claim: Microsoft has not published a date for default enablement of EU and EFTA environments.
claims.quote: Searched: Business Applications Work IQ default existing environments deferred date EU EFTA. Opened default-settings and manage-participation; EU/EFTA remain exceptions with a manual tenant-and-environment enablement route and no default-enablement date.
